case.description: Design a removable joint for a 300 mm inspection hatch on a dry tabletop trough fixture. A technician must open it repeatedly while retaining the existing hatch, rim and seal. All dimensions and observations below are stipulated for this hypothetical fixture.
case.valued_outcome: After ten opening cycles, the closed hatch stays within 1 mm of its marked position, withstands a supplied 20 N sideways pull, and can be reopened by one technician within 30 seconds.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform the hatch or trough.
Keep the full marked inspection opening unobstructed when open.
Use no powered mechanism; loose components must remain recoverable.
The seal must show no new visible tears after testing.
resources: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.
Ninety minutes for fabrication and twenty minutes for observation.
observations: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.

openings.claim: Relocate strap retention into two removable aluminum jaw assemblies: paired strips above the hatch and below an accessible rim, linked by outboard bolts. Rubber pads transmit jaw pressure without direct metal contact. This is an unverified geometry, not deployment.
openings.delta: Replace strap tension with bolted jaw reaction and pad friction. Drill only strips. Each assembly uses two strips, two bolts and two pads; loosen bolts without removing nuts to slide assemblies completely away before opening. Cord bundles removed assemblies and pads outside the marked opening. Technician still fabricates, adjusts, collects, counts and inspects components; maintenance requires checking nuts, pad wear and contact positions each cycle.
openings.prediction: At modest, balanced jaw preload, lateral motion may fall below 1 mm without the observed opposite-corner lift. Nearest rival is tightening the same jaws at the left corner: that attributes retention to greater local compression. Differing observations are lateral displacement versus opposite-corner lift and seal damage. If useful retention requires the rival’s rocking preload, the balanced-pressure hypothesis fails.
openings.probe: First measure rim accessibility, bolt reach and jaw overlap using the ruler; abandon if assembly requires fixture alteration or permanent deformation. Within ninety minutes fabricate only if dimensions fit. Use ten candidate opening/closure/pull trials, timing each reopening and measuring position and corner lift; disturb its final closure with the supplied right-contact card. Use two rival diagnostic trials, one disturbed, within the twelve-trial ceiling. Rival trials cannot establish ten-cycle durability. Inspect seal after every trial; terminate on new tears. Record recoverability and opening clearance, plus final 20 N resistance and reopening time.
assumptions: Accessible underside and sufficient bolt length are indispensable but unspecified.
Strip stiffness and pad friction may be inadequate; rim geometry may prevent sliding removal.
Disturbance may redistribute pressure and defeat alignment even when undisturbed trials pass.

artifact.assessment: Only a bounded probe is proposed. No drilling, cutting, gluing or permanent deformation of hatch or trough is permitted. No power operates the joint. All parts must remain recoverable, the full opening clear, and the seal untorn. Unknown geometry prevents claiming feasibility or performance.

openings.claim: Two removable bolted strip saddles could carry retention formerly supplied by straps, while their visible jaw gaps turn the adverse card into a closure-control signal.
openings.delta: Pair the four strips into two padded edge clamps; drill only strips, place bolts outside hatch/rim edges, and tether removable parts with cord. New carrier: strip-and-bolt interfaces transmit separation resistance into the rim. Card at right contact → increased right jaw gap → marked gap mismatch → technician loosens the left clamp and recenters before retightening. This changes the independent-tightening action; it does not assume the card can be mechanically accommodated.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary independent clamping merely holds the hatch harder and reproduces opposite-corner lift. The proposed response predicts lower opposite-corner lift after gap-triggered adjustment while retaining position and pull resistance. Equal improvement without gap information favors the rival explanation of simple preload reduction. A sham gap signal causing unnecessary adjustment defeats signal specificity.
openings.probe: First verify accessible opposing rim surfaces, bolt reach, recoverable attachment and seal-safe pad locations; absence stops fabrication. Within ninety minutes build one configuration. Use up to twelve closure/pull trials: ten opening cycles, including a sham external gap indication followed by its removal, and a final actual right-card closure; reserve two trials for adjustment comparisons before that final closure. Record position, corner lift, 20 N displacement, reopening time and tears. Test signal cancellation by removing the sham. Reject on binding, false signals, unavailable geometry, any constraint breach or failed final outcomes; stopping alone establishes no feasibility.
assumptions: Rim underside access, edge overlap and supplied bolt lengths are unknown and indispensable.
Gap indication must distinguish card-induced lift from clamp flex or pad compression; this is unproven.

Maintenance costs include checking bolts, pads, marks and tethers each cycle. The technician retains fabrication, interpretation, preload adjustment, recentering, component recovery and seal inspection responsibility.
The seal may not accommodate the card without violating the outcome; no performance is established.

artifact.assessment: One exploratory opening, not deployment. Both relocation and disturbance conversion depend on unverified geometry and informative gap sensing; preserve every hard constraint.

openings.claim: Separate sideways registration from strap compression, and convert the right-contact card into a manual retainer-clearance adjustment.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two bolted, padded removable rim clamps with lateral registration faces; straps retain the hatch against separation. Keep clamps outside the marked opening and release straps to remove the hatch. Adverse card → ruler-confirmed right-contact height increase → technician raises the right retainer clearance by the measured increase before tensioning. The card remains in its assigned contact position. Ordinary strap retention and spacer clearance functions remain intact.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: obtain lateral resistance by increasing left-corner compression. Registration faces should carry the sideways load with lighter strap tension, while the rival risks reproducing opposite-corner lift. Under disturbance, clearance adjustment should avoid extra left compression while preserving horizontal registration. This predicts neither seal continuity nor established performance.
openings.probe: First confirm clamps can grip the actual rim without damage, straps reach their anchors, and every retaining part clears the opening upon release; otherwise stop before fabrication. Drill only strips and tether detachable parts using cord. Within ninety fabrication minutes, build one configuration. Use twelve closure/pull trials: ten numbered opening cycles, then a nominal false-signal trial with an intentionally premature clearance adjustment, then the final right-card trial with measured adjustment. Record horizontal displacement, opposite-corner lift, twenty-newton resistance, reopening time and visible seal condition. In the false-signal trial, cancel the adjustment when no height increase is measured. Reject if cancellation fails, straps escape, clamps slip, clearance cannot accommodate the card, displacement exceeds one millimetre, reopening exceeds thirty seconds, or new tears appear. Rival comparison uses the supplied three trials; additional rival effects remain unknown.
assumptions: Rim geometry permits padded external clamps and strap anchoring; neither accessibility nor reach is supplied.
Available strips and bolts permit registration and adjustable clearance without permanent deformation.
Twenty observation minutes permit twelve measurements; confirm before starting.
A ruler can resolve the relevant height change; otherwise disturbance detection is uninformative.

artifact.assessment: One probe proposal; deployment and reliable performance are unestablished. Missing rim geometry and strap reach are indispensable feasibility uncertainties. The disturbed trial must meet all outcome requirements except seal contact continuity.

openings.claim: Two removable, opposed strip-jaw clamps could carry sideways load through distributed pad friction while avoiding the observed concentrated left-corner preload.
openings.delta: Change the action from corner tightening to matched, small preload increments at opposed mid-edge contacts. Pair the four strips into upper/lower jaws, drill only strips, and use bolts outside the fixture edges. Pad fixture contacts; tie removable assemblies together with cord and park them clear of the opening. Nearest rival: concentrated corner pressure provides sufficient friction despite hatch rocking.
openings.prediction: If distributed preload matters, matched clamps will arrest sideways motion before opposite-corner lift reaches 2 mm, whereas concentrating equivalent tightening at the left contact will cause earlier lift. Tightening is only an approximate preload comparison; it cannot establish equal force.
openings.probe: First verify accessible rim undersides, bolt reach, strip overlap and pad placement without modifying hatch, rim or seal; otherwise park this design. Use one available trial for a reversible left-biased versus matched tightening observation, stopping at visible lift or seal distress. Then use eleven closure/pull trials: initial closure followed by ten opening cycles, with the last closure disturbed by the supplied right-contact card. Record marked displacement under 20 N, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition. All parts must be recoverable and entirely clear when open.
assumptions: Rim access, bolt lengths and strip stiffness permit stable jaws; these are unprovided indispensable geometry/capacity facts.
The initial comparison fits one closure/pull trial and leaves eleven for outcome testing.

Defeat conditions include slipping beyond 1 mm, reopening beyond 30 seconds, seal tearing, obstruction, or inability to fabricate within ninety minutes and observe within twenty. A successful probe would support only this fixture configuration.

artifact.assessment: A conditional mechanical candidate warrants a geometry check before fabrication. Pressure distribution could fail under the right-contact disturbance; no stipulated observation demonstrates clamp feasibility or outcome compliance. This is a probe, not deployment.
